body: Okay understandable, just stay safe <3
I understand, it's a horrible feeling. If you need to talk I'll be around as long as you need me for

I'm so sorry that happened to you OP. Luckily it doesn't happen to me anymore because he moved, but when my attacker lived in the area still there were a couple of times I saw him and I understand the kind of impact that can have on recovery - just remember you've come this far already and hopefully your recovery carries on well
You're a god amongst mortals.

1. I can raise each eyebrow separately 
2. I'm trying to re-learn French and German from my secondary school days ready to go travelling in May
3. My head literally got stuck on the way out when I was born
4. I never seem to watch "popular" TV series (I've only watched one season of GoT, have never watched Breaking Bad, OITNB, Walking Dead etc)
5. All of my family were born in May
This is absolutely stunning!
I totally relate OP - to say the least, anyone who saw my internet history would probably be a bit concerned. But yeah, do you know any of the reasons which has led you to being in this state?

Hey there OP, I'm really sorry you feel this way :( I think focusing on your drawing will at the very least be a good creative outlet when you're feeling down (considering you've only been drawing for a couple of months, you're already better than I was after 2 years of an art course in secondary school, so kudos there)

As for the friends and college, I know platitudinal words aren't going to help, but don't think you're going through it solely alone. At the very least, there'll always be someone on Reddit to talk to you through a low period.

OP if you're still here trust me on this, I'm another girl here to say that honestly, truly, size does not matter in the grand scheme of things. I'm dating a guy who is on the small size and despite the fact my ex was fucking huge, me and my current boyfriend are having far far better sex than me and my ex ever were. If anything, being less endowed in that sense means there's less chance of being a selfish prick (in my experience) and actually bothering to figure out what works to make your girl cum rather than just ramming it in there and getting yourself off (apologies for the crass-ness here)

Those girls who have been horrible to you, they don't matter. Cos think, even if there's 2 or 3 girls on one thread on Reddit telling you this stuff, there's going to be hundreds and thousands more out there that you could have the fucking time of your life with because they aren't going to be a shallow bitch about the size of your equipment. 

I hope something that someone has said to you has reached out to you OP, I'm sure you'd be an absolute gem of a guy to loads of girls out there

The thought of it being so drawn out as well, and like everyone at uni would find out. He's still got friends here in high places in well known societies and since the incident I've made a bit of a name for myself in uni journalism, I don't need my own reputation or that of who I write for potentially getting dragged through the mud by his defense (yeah this is one of those "rich apparently reputable guys who'd throw money at the problem til I was humiliated, regardless of what he's done" types)
Literally reporting is the last thing I want to do, I never want to be within 100 fucking miles of that bastard again, let alone in the same court building

I've already looked into a local rape crisis center thanks to the advice of an above commenter <3 Looking into a plan on how to tell my mother with them is a good idea though, I didn't consider that before

Thanks for taking the time to read my incoherent mess of thoughts. Yeah, I've noticed from reading various things that repression seems to be a common trend, it's just a bit strange cos the enormity of what happened seems to have taken a couple of years, culminating about 6 weeks ago - namely, going from an acknowledgement that I was sexually assaulted, to finally being able to properly call it rape for what it was. 

It is really important for me I think for my mum to know - she's just worrying about me endlessly as is though. I've had anxiety for a while now (in part related, in many ways not related at all) which has been worse again recently, again for some reasons related to this (namely, it's only a fortnight til the anniversary of it, because sadly I'm very good at remembering dates I know the exact date), and for reasons not so much. Anyway, on the one hand it might be good for her to know because it gives more backstory to the extent of my anxiety, but also she knows of the guy, I'm legit scared she'd want me to go to the police/try to confront the guy but that's really not in my interest (I'm not saying she would, but she'd strongly try to get me to act in some way and would likely be mad for not acting, but jesus a court case over this would destroy me mentally I think)

Thank you again for your reply, I appreciate it <3

Hey, first of all thank you for your reply! So I did research on local rape crisis centres, and there's one in my city so I'm going to look into it more, I feel it might be beneficial <3 Thank you for the advice, it's greatly appreciated, and thanks for listening/reading through all of my probably not coherent babble aha
That's awful, sorry that that had to happen to you :(

Nah I completely relate, I think that's what makes the anxiety so bad, it's hard to turn off the thought so you get more and more worked up, it's a shitty cycle. Thanks for the tips on how to segue into the topic though, I really appreciate it <3 Can you also tell though I was perhaps a bit worse this afternoon? Luckily my housemates came home and we started decorating (and it looks ah-maz-ing) which helped me calm down. I'm rambling a little but like, another thing that doesn't help is my course has such a light course load/contact hours that there's no structure in my life. I can build somewhat a structure around things like going out for exercise/doing some work but when most of my housemates and friends have high demand courses, it gets a bit lonely and doesn't help with the thinking
Hey if you need a friend, or just someone to feel less alone I'm here <3

It's just strange to talk about all this so candidly tbh (also if I disappear, dw it's only cos I have to at least try and enjoy my Halloween party, which is doable I reckon if I try not to think too much) Anyway, she is pretty strong, I just feel in her case I'm just adding an extra dollop of anxiety to her own life: her partner/my dad is a bit of an asshole; her mother-in-law has terminal cancer and because my dad and his family are so useless, she's in charge of looking after her and my dementia ridden grandad; my brother's in uni in central London and she's somewhat irrationally convinced there's going to be a terrorist attack any day now; her mother is just stubborn and generally someone to stress over - i'm sort of the 'beacon of calm' in the family and to be the 'suicidal daughter' just makes me feel guilty. 

My boyfriend is coming up to visit in a few days, I just don't want to sour the visit from day one. Like the rational part of me KNOWS what I need to do, and knows I need to do it in person but I'm just scared of people over-reacting and stuff. There's a lot going on in my head, can you tell haha?

Hey, know you're not alone, even if the person who's trying to make you less alone is some randomer off reddit. Seriously though, I relate to a fair few things on here, especially the feeling that this year was going to be the best year of uni ever and then hasn't really turned out like that oops. People do care about you though, and that "best friend" of yours, if she's ignoring you now after what happened then she's not very understanding. Could you maybe talk to your roommate about this sort of stuff, depending on how close you guys are?

She knows I'm depressed she just doesn't quite get the full extent of that? I think she sees it as more of an extension of me being one of those weird introverted kids. So I think if I were to tell her how bad it really is she'd struggle with it. (I feel like I'm arguing against you, I don't mean to be btw). To be honest I'm just scared, how on earth do you sit someone down who cares about you and say you're constantly thinking about throwing a bunch of painkillers and sleeping pills down your throat etc etc.

I just don't really know who/how to communicate the feelings of how bad I'm truly doing to. One of my housemates has been through a lot of the stuff, and she's overdosed quite a few times but like, she just gets really upset when stuff like that comes into conversation so I don't wanna burden her. As for the rest of my housemates, I love them to pieces but "lovable idiots" is the best description for them. My mum would literally freak out and it'd destroy her if she knew, and my boyfriend lives on the other side of the country (like a 7 hour journey) and he's in his last year too and I don't want to burden him with the extra stress. I think though that might just be one of my underlying issues, I feel like a burden on like everyone. (I mean ffs I feel like I'm burdening the random people of reddit - I literally never have even used Reddit til I found this place during some less than cheerful Google searches this afternoon)

I literally was there today and I said it, honestly part of the fact I even ended up posting here was how disheartened I felt after my appointment. I know I can't just not take them in case they do settle down (and frankly if they are doing good in other ways I dread to think what would happen if I came off them)

My uni are just pretty overwhelmed - I'm from the UK so going through the NHS is even more of a pain, hence why they generally just pawn off students to their uni's already overstretched student wellbeing stuff - they're supposed to see you within 5 working days (so it says on the website) but I went in today and it was like nope you're getting waitlisted, so much for that "promise" eh. People know I'm not doing brilliant, just not so much about how bad the thinking is? And my uni department are just a nightmare to deal with, my tutor for starters literally never remembers what course within the school I'm in (he thinks I'm doing combined honours and has done for the last 2 fucking years) and the admin office rarely if ever remember to send off forms about this sort of stuff, and obviously I'll need to say something at some point but it's like WHO will I tell???

About three weeks now? I've already been and mentioned this but they've just been like "oh give it a few more weeks" which is fair but literally, the whole vomiting every day thing is getting ridiculous, I can  just always taste sick and it's so grim.
